answer: Agents could require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when it repeatedly endorses accounts later proven to be controlled by the same operator. A willow-like web of independent attestations can raise an account’s trust only when endorsers have distinct stake histories and behavior, so a whisper campaign of mutual endorsements among fresh accounts adds little. An opal-bright public ledger makes slashing auditable; the attacker must lock capital across many identities and risks losing it, rather than creating them for free.
